specGaps: OBSERVATION SURFACE — where the count lives before 11.7 (draft resolution CORRECTED and pinned). RESOLUTION: schema-observer.hpp exposes two PURE free functions in conductor::router and one struct: `struct SchemaObservation { bool tagged{false}; bool schemaMissing{false}; std::optional<nlohmann::json> declaredSchema; std::optional<bool> schemaConformed; }`; `SchemaObservation observe_request(const RequestTags& tags, const std::string& body)` (schemaConformed left unset); `std::optional<bool> observe_response(const SchemaObservation& observation, bool validateResponses, bool isStream, const std::string& body)`. Router gains exactly two observers mirroring the committed last_request_tags(): `std::optional<SchemaObservation> last_schema_observation() const` (nullopt until one /v1/* request has been handled) and `std::uint64_t schema_missing_count() const` (monotonic since construction, never reset). Task 11.7 consumes the per-request SchemaObservation for its JSONL line and the counter for /conductor/metrics. Tests pin the functions, the struct and the two observers — no ledger file is written by 11.6.

WHAT THE DECLARED SCHEMA IS VALIDATED AGAINST (the gap the draft never asked; the single most load-bearing resolution here). §4.4 says 'the body is validated against the declared schema', but the body is an OpenAI chat.completion envelope while the declared schema describes the model's structured OUTPUT. RESOLUTION: observe_response parses the response body as JSON, then extracts the output text as the FIRST of `choices[0].message.content` (chat completions) or `choices[0].text` (legacy completions) that is present and is a string; that text is parsed as JSON and THAT value is validated against declaredSchema. Verdicts: conforming ⇒ true; output text present but not parseable as JSON, or parseable and rejected by the validator ⇒ false (both are genuine non-conformance by the model); envelope not parseable as JSON, or carrying neither extractable field ⇒ nullopt (unobservable — the router could not find the output, which is not a conformance failure). Rationale: the alternative reading makes every conforming response report false and turns the POC's conformance dataset into noise.

SCHEMA-PRESENCE PREDICATE (draft resolution APPROVED, tightened). The §4.4 bullet says 'response_format/grammar' while the prose says 'response_format (json_schema) or a grammar/json_schema body field'. RESOLUTION: on the FORWARDED body (post-x_conductor-strip, which is what the upstream actually receives), a schema is PRESENT iff the body parses as a JSON object and any of: (a) `response_format` is an object whose `type` == "json_schema" and whose `json_schema.schema` is a non-empty object — declaredSchema = that schema; (b) top-level `grammar` is a non-empty string — declaredSchema stays EMPTY (GBNF, see the next gap); (c) top-level `json_schema` is a non-empty object — declaredSchema = that object. Everything else is schemaMissing, explicitly including: no body at all, a non-JSON body, a JSON body that is not an object, `response_format:{"type":"json_object"}` with no json_schema.schema, `grammar:""`, `json_schema:{}`, and any of the three keys present with a null or wrong-typed value. Each arm and each named negative gets its own SUBCASE.

GRAMMAR-ONLY DECLARATIONS (draft resolution APPROVED). A `grammar` arm declares GBNF, which nlohmann json-schema-validator cannot check. RESOLUTION: arm (b) sets schemaMissing:false (the request DID declare a constraint — counting it missing would inflate the POC's headline number) but leaves declaredSchema empty, so observe_response returns nullopt: conformance is unobservable, exactly as it is for a streamed response. Pinned by its own case in 11.6-conformance-unobservable-null.

THE TAG VALUE PREDICATE (the draft assumed 'engaged optional' == tagged). §4.4 and inject.ts only ever mint `X-Conductor-Schema: required`. RESOLUTION: `tagged` is true iff RequestTags.schema is engaged AND its value equals "required" compared case-insensitively (the sole producer emits lowercase; case-insensitivity costs nothing and closes a proxy-normalization surprise). Any other engaged value is logged at debug and observed as tagged:false — it declares nothing 11.6 knows how to observe, and under the G5 direction the narrow reading is the safe one, since a wider one would let rejectOnMissing:true 400 a value the producer never meant as a schema demand.

'JOURNALED' FOR A C++ ROUTER (draft resolution APPROVED, with one correction). §4.4 says a tagged schema-less request 'is journaled', but conductor's closed journal vocabulary (conductor/core/journal-events.ts EVENTS) has no router-side writer and its 'router-client' component covers only the TS side. RESOLUTION: router-side 'journaled' is one spdlog::warn line per tagged-schema-missing request naming the request's role and group tags and the request path; NOTHING writes journal.jsonl from C++ and NO EVENTS widening is needed. CORRECTION to the draft: this is an implementation obligation, NOT an assertion row — capturing the process-global spdlog default logger from a doctest that runs beside threaded suites is fragile apparatus, so schema_missing_count() and last_schema_observation() are the tested surface.

REJECT-ON-MISSING SCOPE + ORDERING (gap the draft never asked). RESOLUTION: observation runs for EVERY /v1/* request (so last_schema_observation is always the most recent one, uniform with last_request_tags and with what 11.7 must emit a line for), but the rejectOnMissing 400 applies to POST /v1/* ONLY — the exact SG-6 reasoning that keeps GET /v1/models out of admission, since a bodyless read can never carry a schema field and turning it into a 400 is precisely the G5 inversion this task exists to prevent. ORDERING inside handleProxy: planForward → recordTags → observe_request(plan.tags, plan.body) → counter/log → the rejectOnMissing check (POST only; no upstream contact, no admission slot consumed, no queue entry) → admit → relayToUpstream. The counter increments on every tagged-and-missing request whatever rejectOnMissing says: it is an observation, not a consequence of the posture.

400 BODY SHAPE (draft resolution CORRECTED — both predecessor envelopes are now committed, so this is frozen rather than approximated). RESOLUTION: the 400 reuses the committed envelope shape exactly — `{"error":{"message":…,"type":…,"code":…}}`, status 400, Content-Type application/json — with two new constants published from schema-observer.hpp: `kSchemaErrorType = "invalid_request_error"` (the OpenAI-compatible type for a client-side refusal) and `kSchemaMissingCode = "schema_missing"` (a STRING discriminator, following 11.4's newer convention rather than 11.3's integer code). The message MUST contain the resolved observe-header name and the literal string "schema.rejectOnMissing" so an operator reading it learns which config key produced a refusal the base build never makes.

STREAM OBSERVATION vs THE WIRE NOTE (tension the draft did not surface). wire-notes DISCOVERY (i) ends 'llama-router's response observation WILL see streaming responses and must parse SSE, not a single JSON body', which reads as an obligation. RESOLUTION: it is a statement of what response observation WOULD require, and it is exactly why the plan puts stream validation out of scope — §4.4 pins `schemaConformed` as 'true/false/null for streamed' and the 11.6 bullet says 'stream validation is out of scope and recorded in HONEST-LIMITS'. 11.6 therefore does NOT parse, buffer or reassemble SSE: a streamed response records schemaConformed nullopt and the relay is byte-for-byte the one 11.3 already ships. assertions.text: THE WHOLE POINT OF THE TASK (G5). A POST /v1/chat/completions carrying `X-Conductor-Schema: required` (the exact header/value inject.ts headersFor mints) whose JSON body declares NO schema by the pinned predicate — a plain {model, messages} body — is proxied to the stub upstream BYTE-IDENTICALLY (same method, same target, same body bytes, end-to-end headers unchanged: the observation adds, strips and rewrites nothing beyond what 11.3's x_conductor strip already does) and the upstream's status and body return verbatim. Router::last_schema_observation() reports tagged:true, schemaMissing:true, declaredSchema empty; Router::schema_missing_count() advances by exactly one; the request is NEVER rejected under the shipped default config and the stub records exactly one hit for it

Each accepted §4.4 declaration shape is observed as PRESENT, one SUBCASE per arm, asserted through observe_request directly (pure, no server needed): (a) `response_format:{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":…,"schema":<Verdict.schema.json contents>}}` ⇒ schemaMissing:false and declaredSchema == that schema object exactly; (b) a top-level non-empty `grammar` string ⇒ schemaMissing:false and declaredSchema EMPTY (GBNF is not a JSON Schema); (c) a top-level `json_schema` object ⇒ schemaMissing:false and declaredSchema == that object. In every arm the request is tagged, and end-to-end the body still crosses the proxy byte-identically

The negative half of the same predicate, one SUBCASE each, all with the request tagged: an empty body; a non-JSON body; a JSON body that is not an object (an array); `response_format:{"type":"json_object"}` with no json_schema.schema; `response_format:{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"schema":{}}}`; `grammar:""`; `json_schema:{}`; and `response_format`/`grammar`/`json_schema` present but null or of the wrong JSON type — every one observes schemaMissing:true with declaredSchema empty, and NONE of them is rejected or mutated under the default config

An UNTAGGED request — no X-Conductor-Schema header and no `schema` key in an x_conductor body field, plus the boundary case of the header present with an EMPTY value, which 11.3's readHeaderTag already drops — is untouched whatever its body shape: proxied byte-identically, observed tagged:false and schemaMissing:false, schema_missing_count() unchanged, no response validation attempted even when the body DOES carry a response_format schema. This holds identically under schema.rejectOnMissing:true — the opt-in 400 applies ONLY to tagged requests — and a request whose schema tag carries some value other than "required" is likewise observed tagged:false

schema_missing_count() counts tagged-and-missing requests and nothing else: across one Router serving a mixed sequence of six requests through the stub — tagged+missing, tagged+response_format schema, untagged+missing, tagged+missing, untagged+schema, tagged+grammar — the counter reads exactly 2, it is monotonic (it never decreases across the sequence and is not reset by any request), it starts at 0 on a freshly constructed Router, and last_schema_observation() reflects the LAST request only (nullopt before any /v1/* request has been handled, mirroring last_request_tags())

The tag is read through 11.3's ALREADY-NORMALIZED RequestTags.schema, never re-read from the wire: a Router built with config.schema.observeHeader = "X-Fleet-Schema" observes a request carrying `X-Fleet-Schema: required` as tagged, while a request carrying only the shipped "X-Conductor-Schema" name under that same config is observed UNTAGGED; and with the shipped config a request whose tag arrives only via the x_conductor body fallback (`{"x_conductor":{"schema":"required"}}`, stripped before forwarding) is observed tagged with the presence predicate evaluated against the POST-STRIP body the upstream actually receives. The shipped "X-Conductor-Schema" is config data, not a hardcoded constant, so this row is asserted end-to-end through the real Router

A TAGGED request declaring Verdict.schema.json (read from src/tests/schemas/, never hand-copied) whose stub upstream answers with a single NON-STREAM chat.completion body records a conformance verdict WITHOUT touching the response: with `choices[0].message.content` holding the JSON text of a conforming Verdict ({findingId, upheld, reasoning}) the observation records schemaConformed:true; with content holding a Verdict missing `reasoning`, carrying an extra property (additionalProperties:false), or holding text that is not JSON at all, it records schemaConformed:false; and in EVERY one of those cases the response body returns byte-verbatim with the upstream's status and Content-Type — never wrapped, never re-serialized, never re-statused. The legacy `choices[0].text` shape yields the identical verdicts

schemaConformed is recorded as an EMPTY optional — unobservable, distinct from false — in each of these cases, one SUBCASE each, with the response still returning byte-verbatim every time: the request was untagged; the request was tagged but declared no schema; the request declared grammar only (arm b, no JSON Schema to validate against); config.schema.validateResponses is false (the shipped default is true, so this row builds the config explicitly); the response body is not parseable JSON; the response body parses but carries neither `choices[0].message.content` nor `choices[0].text` as a string (an embeddings body, an error body, an empty choices array); and the request-embedded schema is one nlohmann json-schema-validator CANNOT COMPILE (e.g. `{"type": 42}`) — that last case is load-bearing G5: a malformed declared schema is logged and observed as unobservable, and can never turn a request the direct path would have served into a failure

A tagged request declaring a schema whose stub upstream answers `Content-Type: text/event-stream` with several `data: {...}` chunks and a terminating `data: [DONE]` (the shape wire-notes DISCOVERY (i) pins for real fan-out traffic) passes through exactly as 11.3's relay already delivers it — the client observes the chunk bytes and their order unchanged, the SSE content type preserved, and the chunks arriving incrementally rather than as one buffered write — while the observation records schemaConformed as an EMPTY optional. No chunk is buffered for inspection, no stream is reassembled, and no validator is invoked on streamed bytes

With schema.rejectOnMissing:true (the non-default posture, reachable by config change and never by a code path) a TAGGED POST /v1/* missing its schema field is answered 400 with Content-Type application/json and a parseable body `{"error":{"message":…,"type":"invalid_request_error","code":"schema_missing"}}` whose message contains BOTH the resolved observe-header name and the literal "schema.rejectOnMissing"; the stub upstream records ZERO hits for it, no admission slot is consumed and schema_missing_count() still advances (the refusal is a posture, the count is an observation). Under that same config a tagged request WITH a schema field proxies normally, an untagged request proxies normally, and a tagged schema-less GET /v1/models proxies normally — the 400 is POST-only, for the same G5 reason SG-6 keeps GET out of admission

The shipped posture is observe-not-enforce, asserted as BEHAVIOUR and not merely as a field value: the §2.2 document verbatim (config_test.cpp's kSection22ConfigText, plan lines 636-670) parsed through Task 11.2's parseRouterConfig against the exported RouterConfig.schema.json yields schema.observeHeader "X-Conductor-Schema", schema.validateResponses true and schema.rejectOnMissing FALSE; a config document omitting rejectOnMissing entirely also yields false; and a Router constructed from that parsed §2.2 config — with only listen.port redirected to the ephemeral-port seam and upstream redirected to the stub, the schema block untouched — proxies a tagged schema-less request through to the stub with the upstream's status rather than answering 400. The plan bullet's 'a test asserts the shipped default config has it false' is an executing doctest, not a comment

The plan's single-source/two-validator discipline (lines 2069-2075) holds from the C++ side: an exported §2 schema read verbatim from src/tests/schemas/ (Verdict.schema.json, and Findings.schema.json as a second case) compiles into the linked nlohmann json-schema-validator without throwing despite carrying no $schema key, and its accept/reject verdicts on a conforming value, a value missing a required property, and a value with an extra property under additionalProperties:false are exactly the ones the §2 schema states — so the router's full validator and conductor/core/types.ts's subset validator cannot disagree about the same payload

SHRUNK-SCOPE NOTE (the branch-b-plan.md lines 91-94 scoping binding): the task appends to docs/build/honest-limits-pending.md — the accumulator Task 15.1 folds into HONEST-LIMITS.md alongside §9's limits — that response observation is INERT on the real fan-out path, citing conductor/adapter/wire-notes.md rather than re-deriving it: opencode 1.18.15's session.prompt issues STREAMING provider requests (DISCOVERY (i)), so every fan-out schemaConformed is unobservable and 11.6 parses no SSE; and the prompt-format DRIFT records that NO schema'd body field is emitted at all, so every tagged fan-out request is expected to observe schemaMissing:true. The router's schema-conformance dataset is therefore the request-side counter, and the router is justified by scheduling and metrics alone.
